learn.rule: A thesis makes a claim someone could argue with and previews your reasons. A conclusion says the thesis again in fresh words and tells why it matters.
learn.ruleEs: Una tesis hace una afirmación que alguien podría debatir y anticipa tus razones. Una conclusión repite la tesis con palabras nuevas y dice por qué importa.
learn.model: Middle schools should start after 8:30 a.m. because teenagers learn better when they get enough sleep.
learn.notice: Notice that the sentence takes a side with should and gives a reason with because.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the strongest thesis about school start times?

options.text: This essay is about school start times and why they matter to students.
Some schools start at 7:30 a.m., and others start at 9:00 a.m., depending on the district and the grade.
Middle schools should start after 8:30 a.m. because teenagers learn better when they get enough sleep.
School start times are interesting and affect many families every day.

items.why: A strong thesis takes a clear side and gives a reason. The other choices announce a topic, state a plain fact, or stay vague.
items.whyEs: Una tesis fuerte toma una postura clara y da una razón. Las otras opciones anuncian un tema, dan un dato simple o son vagas.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that makes an arguable claim about sleep and school.

options.text: Middle school students should have a later start time.
Many schools start before 8:00 a.m.
Sleep is the most important healthy habit for teenagers.
During sleep, the body rests and repairs itself.
Schools should teach students how sleep affects learning.

items.why: An arguable claim is something a reasonable person could disagree with. The other two sentences are facts that no one would argue about.
items.whyEs: Una afirmación debatible es algo con lo que una persona razonable podría no estar de acuerdo. Las otras dos oraciones son datos que nadie debatiría.

items.prompt: Which thesis also previews its reasons?

options.text: Schools should start later in the morning than they do now.
Schools should start later because students will learn better, feel healthier, and arrive more alert.
I think later start times are better for most students in my town.
Later start times are a topic that many people discuss at school board meetings.

items.why: A thesis that previews names the claim and the reasons the essay will cover. The others make a claim with no reasons or no claim at all.
items.whyEs: Una tesis que anticipa nombra la afirmación y las razones que cubrirá el ensayo. Las otras no dan razones o ni siquiera hacen una afirmación.

items.prompt: Complete the conclusion by choosing words that restate the thesis.
parts: students stay healthy and alert, so schools
items.model: In conclusion, starting school later would help students stay healthy and alert, so schools should consider the change.
items.why: A conclusion restates the claim and tells why it matters. Would help and should match the thesis, and the other words reverse it.
items.whyEs: Una conclusión repite la afirmación y dice por qué importa. Would help y should coinciden con la tesis, y las otras palabras la invierten.

items.prompt: Which sentence restates this thesis in fresh words? Thesis: 'Middle schools should start later because teenagers need more sleep to learn.'

options.text: Middle schools should start later because teenagers need more sleep to learn.
Sleep is important, and many people care about it.
Now I have finished writing about school start times.
Because well-rested teens learn best, schools would serve them better with a later first bell.

items.why: A fresh restatement keeps the same claim and reason in new words. It does not copy the thesis, shrink it to something vague, or only say the essay is over.
items.whyEs: Una nueva formulación mantiene la misma afirmación y razón con palabras diferentes. No copia la tesis, no la reduce a algo vago ni solo dice que el ensayo terminó.

write.prompt: Write a thesis and a closing sentence. Prompt: Should schools have a daily quiet reading time?
write.promptEs: Escribe una tesis y una oración final. Tema: ¿Deberían las escuelas tener un tiempo diario de lectura en silencio?
write.text: Prompt: Should schools have a daily quiet reading time? Essay frame: Thesis (claim + reasons) then Closing (fresh words + why it matters).

write.model: Schools should set aside twenty minutes every day for quiet reading because it builds focus, improves vocabulary, and gives students a calm break. In conclusion, daily reading time is a small change that helps every student learn.

familyTalk.en: Pick a question your family disagrees about, such as a weekend plan. Each person states a claim with because.
familyTalk.es: Elijan una pregunta sobre la que su familia no esté de acuerdo, como un plan de fin de semana. Cada persona expresa una afirmación con because.

teacherTip.en: Have students test each thesis with: could someone disagree, and did I give a reason?
teacherTip.es: Pide que prueben cada tesis con: ¿alguien podría no estar de acuerdo? ¿di una razón?

learn.rule: A thesis makes a claim someone could argue with and previews your reasons. A conclusion says the thesis again in fresh words and tells why it matters.
learn.ruleEs: Una tesis hace una afirmación que alguien podría debatir y anticipa tus razones. Una conclusión repite la tesis con palabras nuevas y dice por qué importa.
learn.model: Public libraries remain essential because they give everyone free access to information, technology, and community programs.
learn.notice: The word essential makes a claim, and the three things after because are the reasons.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the strongest thesis about public libraries?

options.text: Public libraries are places with books, tables, and quiet rooms.
My essay will explain libraries and what they offer to the public.
Libraries have shelves, desks, and many kinds of books for readers.
Public libraries remain essential because they give everyone free access to information, technology, and community programs.

items.why: The strongest thesis takes a stance, essential, and previews three reasons. The others are plain facts or an announcement.
items.whyEs: La tesis más fuerte toma una postura, essential, y anticipa tres razones. Las otras son datos simples o un anuncio.

items.prompt: Pick the sentences that are arguable claims, not just facts.

options.text: Many libraries lend e-books and audiobooks.
Every town should have a public library.
Libraries offer more than books, and that makes them essential.
Libraries have shelves, desks, and computers.
Reading a printed book is a better way to learn than watching a video.

items.why: A claim can be debated because it states an opinion or judgment. Lending e-books and having desks are facts.
items.whyEs: Una afirmación se puede debatir porque expresa una opinión o un juicio. Prestar libros electrónicos y tener escritorios son datos.

items.prompt: Which thesis is too vague to guide an essay?

options.text: Libraries should stay open late because working families need quiet places to study and use computers.
Public libraries help communities by lending books, offering classes, and providing internet access.
Libraries are good.

items.why: Libraries are good gives no clear claim and no reasons, so a reader cannot tell what the essay will say. The other two are specific.
items.whyEs: Libraries are good no da una afirmación clara ni razones, así que el lector no sabe qué dirá el ensayo. Las otras dos son específicas.

items.prompt: Choose the words that complete the thesis frame.
parts: they offer free books, computers, and classes to everyone.
items.model: Public libraries deserve our support because they offer free books, computers, and classes to everyone.
items.why: Deserve states the claim and because introduces the reasons. The other words do not make a logical thesis.
items.whyEs: Deserve expresa la afirmación y because introduce las razones. Las otras palabras no forman una tesis lógica.

items.prompt: Which sentence restates this thesis in fresh words? Thesis: 'Libraries remain essential because they offer free resources to everyone.'

options.text: Libraries remain essential because they offer free resources to everyone.
Libraries have books, tables, and computers for visitors.
Free access to information, technology, and programs is why communities still need their libraries.
That is all I have to say about libraries.

items.why: A restatement says the same idea in new words. Copying the thesis, shrinking it, or ending the essay does not.
items.whyEs: Una nueva formulación dice la misma idea con otras palabras. Copiar la tesis, reducirla o terminar el ensayo no lo logra.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence explains why the library thesis matters?
items.text: In conclusion, libraries give everyone free access to learning.

options.text: Libraries have a lot of books, and some are very old.
I hope you liked my essay about libraries.
Another place to visit is the museum downtown.
Without libraries, many people would lose their only chance to use a computer or find a quiet place to study, so communities should protect them.

items.why: A strong closing tells why the claim matters to real people. The other choices add a small fact, ask for approval, or change the topic.
items.whyEs: Un buen cierre dice por qué la afirmación importa a las personas. Las otras opciones agregan un dato pequeño, piden aprobación o cambian de tema.

write.promptEs: Escribe una tesis y una oración final. Tema: ¿Deberían los estudiantes aprender a cocinar en la escuela?

familyTalk.en: Debate a small question at home, such as which meal is best for a celebration. Give a claim and three reasons.
familyTalk.es: Debatan en casa una pregunta pequeña, como cuál es la mejor comida para una celebración. Den una afirmación y tres razones.

teacherTip.en: Show a vague thesis and a strong thesis side by side and let students name the difference.
teacherTip.es: Muestra una tesis vaga y una fuerte lado a lado y deja que los estudiantes nombren la diferencia.

sets.title: A Case for City Trees
sets.titleEs: Un argumento a favor de los árboles urbanos

learn.rule: A thesis makes a claim someone could argue with and previews your reasons. A conclusion says the thesis again in fresh words and tells why it matters.
learn.ruleEs: Una tesis hace una afirmación que alguien podría debatir y anticipa tus razones. Una conclusión repite la tesis con palabras nuevas y dice por qué importa.
learn.model: Cities should plant more trees because shade cools streets, roots absorb rainwater, and leaves clean the air.
learn.notice: The thesis makes one claim and previews three science reasons.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the strongest thesis about trees in cities?

options.text: Trees are tall plants with trunks, branches, and leaves.
I will tell you about city trees and why they are interesting.
Cities have many buildings, roads, and bridges that fill their streets.
Cities should plant more trees because shade cools streets, roots absorb rainwater, and leaves clean the air.

items.why: A strong thesis states a position and previews the reasons that will follow. The others give a fact, announce a topic, or describe cities.
items.whyEs: Una tesis fuerte expresa una posición y anticipa las razones que seguirán. Las otras dan un dato, anuncian un tema o describen las ciudades.

items.prompt: Pick the sentences that are arguable claims, not just facts.

options.text: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
Every city street should have shade trees.
A shade tree can lower the temperature of the ground beneath it.
Parks with large trees make neighborhoods healthier places to live.
Planting trees is the most effective way to cool a neighborhood.

items.why: Claims state a position that could be argued and then supported with evidence. Facts about carbon dioxide and shade are already proven.
items.whyEs: Las afirmaciones expresan una posición que se puede debatir y luego apoyar con evidencia. Los datos sobre el dióxido de carbono y la sombra ya están comprobados.

items.prompt: Which sentence announces a topic instead of making a claim?

options.text: City trees deserve protection because they cool, clean, and calm neighborhoods.
In this essay, I will discuss trees in cities.
Cities should plant more trees.

items.why: An announcement tells what the essay is about but takes no position. A thesis tells what the writer believes.
items.whyEs: Un anuncio dice de qué trata el ensayo, pero no toma una posición. Una tesis dice lo que cree quien escribe.

items.prompt: Complete the conclusion so it restates the thesis.
parts: city life by cooling streets and cleaning the air, so every community
make room for more of them.
items.model: In conclusion, planting trees improves city life by cooling streets and cleaning the air, so every community should make room for more of them.
items.why: The conclusion repeats the claim in new words and says what to do. Improves and should keep the same position as the thesis.
items.whyEs: La conclusión repite la afirmación con otras palabras y dice qué hacer. Improves y should mantienen la misma posición que la tesis.

items.prompt: Which sentence restates this thesis in fresh words? Thesis: 'Cities should plant more trees because they cool streets and clean the air.'

options.text: Cities should plant more trees because they cool streets and clean the air.
Adding trees to urban neighborhoods would make them cooler and healthier places to live.
Trees are green and grow in many places.
Now you know a lot about trees in cities.

items.why: A fresh restatement keeps the same claim and reasons in new words. It does not copy the thesis or give up the claim.
items.whyEs: Una nueva formulación mantiene la misma afirmación y razones con palabras diferentes. No copia la tesis ni abandona la afirmación.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence tells why the tree thesis matters?
items.text: In conclusion, cities that plant more trees become cooler, healthier places.

options.text: As summers get hotter, shade trees may protect people's health and make city life more comfortable for everyone.
Trees come in many shapes and sizes, and some live for centuries.
Thank you for reading this essay about city trees.
Next, I will write about parks and playgrounds.

items.why: A strong closing connects the claim to people's lives. The other choices state a plain fact, thank the reader, or change topics.
items.whyEs: Un cierre fuerte conecta la afirmación con la vida de las personas. Las otras opciones dan un dato simple, agradecen al lector o cambian de tema.

write.model: Every school should have a vegetable garden because gardens teach science, encourage healthy eating, and bring students together. In short, a school garden grows both fresh food and curiosity about how living things work.

familyTalk.en: Walk around your neighborhood and pick one change you would argue for, such as more shade or a new bench. State a claim with reasons.
familyTalk.es: Caminen por su vecindario y elijan un cambio que defenderían, como más sombra o una banca nueva. Expresen una afirmación con razones.

teacherTip.en: Have partners trade theses and underline the claim and the reasons in each other's work.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas intercambien tesis y que subrayen la afirmación y las razones en el trabajo del otro.
